notes: Initial TVM FFI baseline with dynamic smem - all 100 workloads passed
Iteration 1: cached per-timestep decayed shared state to avoid recomputing g * state during the update loop
Iteration 2: row-blocked the vi loop in tiles of 8 rows so multiple reductions share each CTA-wide synchronization phase
Iteration 3: split the recurrent state over 16-row tiles so each CTA owns one (seq, v_head, row_tile) and the launch exposes 8x more prefill blocks
Iteration 4: hoisted per-timestep gate scalar work so each CTA computes g and beta once per token instead of once per thread
Iteration 5: switch underfilled launches to 8-row tiles when the default 16-row prefill grid would launch fewer than one block per SM
Iteration 6: add a 4-row prefill tile fallback when the 8-row launch would still expose fewer than roughly two blocks per SM

Iteration 7: broaden the 8-row launch heuristic so the 16-row prefill path only runs once it can expose roughly two blocks per SM; revert because mean speedup regressed versus the latest comparable quick baseline

Iteration 8: hoist the per-row residual scalar beta * (v - kdot) into the single-thread reduction phase and reuse it from shared memory in the update loop; revert because mean speedup regressed versus the latest comparable quick baseline

Iteration 9: add a 2-row prefill tile fallback when the existing 4-row launch would still expose fewer than roughly two blocks per SM; revert because mean speedup regressed versus the latest comparable quick baseline

Iteration 10: keep each thread's 4-row prefill state tile in registers instead of shared memory during the recurrent loop; revert because correctness held but mean speedup regressed versus the latest comparable quick baseline
Iteration 11 (Ralph loop 9): remove the redundant end-of-timestep CTA barrier because the next timestep already synchronizes before reusing shared scalars and row tiles

Iteration 12 (Ralph loop 10): parallelize the per-tile row epilogues across warp 0 instead of serializing both kdot and output reductions through tid == 0; revert because correctness held but mean speedup regressed versus the latest comparable quick baseline

Iteration 13 (Ralph loop 11): route longer 2-sequence workloads to the existing 8-row prefill kernel via a total-seq-len dispatch split; revert because correctness held but mean speedup regressed versus the latest comparable quick baseline

Iteration 14 (Ralph loop 12): fuse the output path algebraically by computing q @ temp alongside k @ temp and using q·k * residual to avoid the second per-row reduction; revert because the quick Modal benchmark produced INCORRECT_NUMERICAL on 17/100 workloads versus the latest comparable quick baseline mean_speedup 105.33745939876322

Iteration 15 (Ralph loop 13): fuse the output path algebraically by accumulating q @ temp and q·k during the k @ temp pass so the kernel can emit outputs without the second per-row cross-warp reduction; revert because the quick Modal benchmark produced INCORRECT_NUMERICAL on 16/100 workloads versus the latest comparable quick baseline mean_speedup 105.33745939876322

Iteration 16 (Ralph loop 14): broaden the 2-row micro-tile fallback so the current 4-row prefill path switches to 2-row tiles whenever it would still expose fewer than roughly four blocks per SM; commit because correctness held and mean speedup improved versus the latest comparable quick baseline 105.33745939876322
